The proof of Theorem <REF_0001> uses that <MATH_0001> and <MATH_0002>
are separated over <MATH_0003> in two places. First, the proof uses this in showing
<MATH_0004> is representable by algebraic spaces.
This use of the assumption can be entirely avoided by proving
that <MATH_0005> is representable by applying the theorem in the
separated case to the triples
<MATH_0006>, <MATH_0007>, and <MATH_0008>
found in Remark <REF_0002> (this is the usual bootstrap
procedure for the diagonal). Thus the proof of
Lemma <REF_0003> is the only
place in our proof of Theorem <REF_0004>
where we really need to use that <MATH_0009> is separated.
The reader checks that we use the assumption only to obtain
the morphism <MATH_0010>. The existence of <MATH_0011> can be shown,
using results in the literature, if <MATH_0012> is quasi-separated, see
More on Morphisms of Spaces, Remark
<REF_0005>.
We conclude the theorem holds as stated with
``separated'' replaced by ``quasi-separated''. If we ever need this
we will precisely state and carefully prove this here.
